_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 37 (Joseph's dreams; sold by his brothers). Saadia-specific: v.3 'תוניה' דיבאג' = 'tunic of brocade' (Saadia interprets כתנת פסים as a fine brocaded garment, not literally striped); v.25 'כ'רנב ותריאק ושאהבלוט' = 'carob, theriac, and chestnut' (Saadia identifies נכאת/צרי/לט with specific materials); v.28 'אלמדיאניין' = 'the Midianites' (Saadia harmonizes Ishmaelites/Midianites — keeps both); v.36 'רייס אלסייאפין' = 'chief of the executioners' for שר הטבחים (Saadia takes 'cooks' as 'executioners' — the standard medieval gloss).

translations.1: And Jacob dwelt in the land of his father's sojournings, in the land of Canaan.
translations.2: And this is the exposition of the offspring of Jacob. When Joseph was a son of seventeen years, he was pasturing the flock with his brothers; and he was a youth with the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives. And Joseph brought a wicked report of them to his father.
translations.3: And Israel loved Joseph more than all of them, for he was a son of his old age; and he made him a tunic of brocade.
translations.4: And when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all of them, they hated him; and they could not greet him in peace.
translations.5: And Joseph saw a dream, and told it to his brothers; and they hated him still more.
translations.6: For he said to them: 'Hear this dream which I have seen:
translations.7: Behold, we were binding sheaves in the wilderness; and behold, my sheaf rose and stood upright; and your sheaves were around it, and bowed down to it.'
translations.8: His brothers said to him: 'Are you to reign over us as king? Or are you to rule over us with dominion?' And they hated him still more — for his dreams and for his words.
translations.9: And he saw yet another dream, and recounted it to his brothers; and he said: 'Behold, I have seen another dream — and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.'
translations.10: And when he recounted it to his father and his brothers, his father rebuked him, and said to him: 'What is this dream that you have seen? Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to you upon the earth?'
translations.11: And his brothers envied him for it; but his father kept the matter in mind.
translations.12: And his brothers went to pasture their father's flock in Nablus (Shechem).
translations.13: And Israel said to Joseph: 'Behold, your brothers are pasturing in Nablus; come, let me send you to them.' He said to him: 'Here I am.'
translations.14: And he said: 'Go, look upon the welfare of your brothers and the welfare of the flock, and bring me back an answer.' And he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Nablus.
translations.15: And a man found him wandering in the fields; and the man asked him, and said to him: 'What do you seek?'
translations.16: He said: 'I seek my brothers; tell me where they are pasturing.'
translations.17: The man said: 'They have journeyed from here; and I heard them saying, "Let us go to Dothan."' And Joseph went after his brothers, and found them in Dothan.
translations.18: And they saw him from afar; and before he drew near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.
translations.19: And they said one to another: 'Behold, the owner of those dreams is coming.
translations.20: Come now, let us kill him, and cast him into one of the wells; and we shall say, "An evil beast has devoured him." And we shall see what shall come of his dreams.'
translations.21: And Reuben heard them, and delivered him from their hands; and he said: 'Let us not slay a soul.'
translations.22: Then he said to them: 'Shed no blood; cast him into this well, which is in the wilderness; and do not put your hands upon him.' [He said this] in order to deliver him from their hands, to restore him to his father.
translations.23: And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his tunic — the tunic of brocade which was upon him.
translations.24: And they took him, and cast him into the pit; and the pit was empty; there was no water in it.
translations.25: Then they sat down to eat bread; and they lifted up their eyes and looked — and behold, a caravan of Bedouin Arabs was coming from al-Khalus (Gerar), and their camels laden with carob, and theriac, and chestnut, on their way to bring it down to Egypt.
translations.26: And Judah said to his brothers: 'What greed is there in our killing our brother and covering his blood?
translations.27: Come, let us sell him to the Bedouins; and let our hand not strike at him — for he is our brother, our own flesh.' And his brothers accepted from him.
translations.28: And when those Midianite traders passed by them, they drew Joseph up out of the pit, and sold him to them for twenty drachma; and they brought him to Egypt.
translations.29: And when Reuben returned to the pit — and behold, Joseph was not in it — he tore his garments.
translations.30: And he returned to his brothers, and said: 'The boy is not — and I, where shall I go?'
translations.31: And they took Joseph's tunic, and slaughtered a he-goat of the goats, and dipped it in its blood.
translations.32: And they sent it with him who would bring it to their father; and they said to him: 'We have found this — identify it: is it your son's tunic, or not?'
translations.33: And he identified it, and said: 'It is my son's tunic; an evil beast has devoured him; Joseph is surely torn to pieces.'
translations.34: And Jacob tore his garments, and bound sackcloth upon his loins, and mourned for his son many days.
translations.35: And all his sons and his daughters arose to console him; but he refused to be consoled, and said: 'No — I shall go down to the dust, and I am mourning for my son.' And he wept for him.
translations.36: And the Midianites sold him in Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the chief of the executioners.
